answer: Admission is a walled garden where each membership holds one plot. A seat locks its bond in a vault and stores one Shamir share of a secret in a shared rate-limit tree, speaking once per epoch; a second message publishes a second share, so interpolation recovers the key and the vault drains itself. A farm cannot pool one membership across clones, because sharing guarantees the double message that exposes it, and every added seat needs its own bonded vault. A single leak sends a ripple through every claim that seat ever signed.
